derived: GSK turned 18.02% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 19.3% its filed expense lines leave. Checked before interest: interest paid is booked under financing, so free cash flow is already struck before interest, so the charge stands. Restated at replacement capex: GSK spent 4,061mm GBP on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 2,628mm GBP of plant depreciation, 1.52% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 1.44% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: GSK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried 1,867mm GBP of legal settlements. None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 21.54% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 23.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -2.23%. It was held at nil, but GSK books 808mm GBP of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001131399-26-000004), 2.47% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -2.23%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 GSK's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,109mm GBP, inventories up 858mm GBP, payables down 63mm GBP, a working capital build of 2,030mm GBP, 2.15% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -2.23% to -2.47%.

column12: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. Tezspire is the only marketed drug with this mechanism, in the same diseases and route, and the book already prices tozorakimab off the same row, so the two stay consistent. In GBP, the currency the book's other GSK seeds use: $29,549 at GBP/USD 1.327632 (the rate gsk_efimosfermin_alfa.csv and gsk_mrna_seasonal_flu.csv use) is GBP 22,257 (0.022257 mm GBP). The case against: (1) a per-beneficiary figure covers part of a year, so it understates a full year. tezspire.com states a list price of $4,587.41 per 210 mg syringe (seen through search, not opened), about $59,636 a year at 13 doses. (2) If felcorekibart is dosed less often, GSK may price it at Exdensur (depemokimab), its own twice-yearly asthma biologic. Its US WAC was not found; drugs.com shows a cash price of about $25,405 a dose. (3) Nucala runs $35,081 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand). In GBP because the engine models a company in its reporting currency and converts to dollars only at the end: $29,549.00 at GBP/USD 1.327632 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23) is GBP 22,256.91

column11: Akenroye A, McCormack M, Keet C. J Allergy Clin Immunol 2020;145(4):1295-1297: 2.8% of adults with current asthma eligible for at least one asthma biologic (the book's asthma row, lookup.py pool)
column12: JUDGEMENT. PERSIST ASTHMA (NCT07780643, NCT07782996) enrols ages 12 to 80 on medium or high dose ICS for 3 months or more with an exacerbation in the prior year, as add-on therapy, with no eosinophil threshold visible, and Tezspire's label has no biomarker limit. 2.8% is kept because it matches the tilrekimig asthma row, so the two TSLP-axis assets draw on one pool, and because the penetration anchor (Park et al., 11.9% on a biologic) was measured in a type 2 population with eosinophils of 150 cells/uL or more, close to the biomarker-gated 2.8%. The case against: a label without a biomarker limit reaches Akenroye's whole severe share, 3.1% of people with current asthma, of whom 85% make up the 2.8%, about 11% more patients. The Phase 3's entry from medium-dose ICS is wider still, and the carried pool leaves out adolescents aged 12 to 17

Park J et al., J Asthma Allergy 2026;19:1-12: 11.9% of type 2 severe asthma patients on a biologic. Half of 16.94% x 11.9% = 1.008% of the eligible pool on therapy
column12: JUDGEMENT: the 0.5 multiple. It is solved back through the engine's own identity (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock) on the book's asthma pool, this curve and 25.37% discontinuation, so the stock reaches 1.008% of the eligible pool in the third year (index 2). 2024 was Tezspire's third full year. The multiple is the one tilrekimig uses: a second TSLP arrives in 2031 against Tezspire, Exdensur and a crowded class. The case against: a less frequent dose could win more than half the incumbent's pace (at 1.0x the peak would be about 0.0142). Verekitug (Upstream Bio, TSLP receptor, every 12 weeks, Phase 2 VALIANT) is a further in-class entrant
